marble.name: The Carbon Cycle
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Describe the carbon cycle, tracing carbon through photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, and combustion, and explain the role of each process
marble.prompt: If you was asked where the carbon in a wooden table came from originally, could they trace its journey through the carbon cycle — from the atmosphere, through a plant, into the tree, and back out again?

cluster.summary: Your child is exploring how living things interact with their environment — learning about different habitats, simple food chains, and the difference between living, dead, and never-alive things.

misconceptions: Thinking carbon is 'used up' or created, rather than conserved and cycled between reservoirs.
Believing plants only add oxygen and animals only add CO₂, missing that plants also respire and that respiration/combustion/decomposition all return CO₂.
Assuming rising atmospheric CO₂ means carbon is newly appearing, rather than being moved rapidly from fossil stores into the air faster than it is removed.
Treating photosynthesis and respiration as unrelated to a global cycle, not seeing them as the balancing biological fluxes.
representations: Carbon-cycle diagram with each process arrowed and tagged +CO₂ / −CO₂
A followable carbon atom moving through photosynthesis→feeding→respiration→decomposition→combustion
Reservoir stocks (atmosphere, living things, fossil fuels) with an atmospheric-CO₂ meter
Balanced-scale image of removal vs return fluxes, tipped by human activity
authoredAnswer: Most of the tree's material and carbon came from carbon dioxide in the AIR, not the soil — captured by photosynthesis and built into glucose and then wood. That carbon returns to the air as CO2 through respiration (of the tree itself, of animals that eat it, and of decomposers), through combustion if the wood burns, and through decomposition when it dies. Carbon cycles — it is not used up.

wrongAnswers.wrong: The tree's wood came mostly from nutrients and material it took up from the soil.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Attributes the wood's mass to soil nutrients or material taken up by the roots.
wrongAnswers.fix: Reteach photosynthesis as building matter from CO2 and water; the soil supplies only small amounts of mineral nutrients, not the bulk mass.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Denies plants respire; cannot complete the cycle from the tree itself.
wrongAnswers.fix: Establish that plants respire all the time (as well as photosynthesising), releasing CO2 — use the aerobic respiration equation to make the return path concrete.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Cannot name any route back to the atmosphere, or says the carbon is gone once in the tree.
wrongAnswers.fix: Close the loop: name respiration, combustion and decomposition as returns; carbon is conserved and recirculated, never destroyed.
